chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And let not the witnesses refuse [to testify],' he said: 'Before the martyrdom.' And regarding His saying: 'And whoever conceals it, then indeed he is a sinner in his heart,' he said: 'After the martyrdom.'

key_terms.آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ: He is a sinner in his heart

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in meaning of 'shuhada' before and after martyrdom according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the temporal scope of the command to witnesses not to refuse testimony by linking 'before martyrdom' to the duty of active testimony and 'after martyrdom' to the sin of concealing the truth of one's death. This exegesis highlights the transition from the physical act of witnessing to the internal spiritual state of the heart, emphasizing that concealment of the truth remains a sin even after the witness has passed. Such interpretation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of truthfulness from life to death.
